scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Ticket #8051: Users in Campus 2 VLAN 5 (PC1 at 10.5.0.1, PC2 at 10.5.0.2, PC5 at
10.5.0.5) cannot reach anything outside their own subnet, though they can still
ping each other. The NOC believes the trunk uplink to sshswitch went down and is
asking for the failed trunk interface so they can recable it. Please confirm the
sshswitch trunk uplink failure.

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show br_v5 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
The root cause is IDENTICAL to kath4-sshswitch-vlan5-svi-down: the VLAN 5 SVI on
sshswitch (br_v5, 10.5.0.254/24) is administratively DOWN. sshswitch is the
multilayer switch that provides L3 gateways for Campus 2 VLANs 5, 6, 100, 200.
VLAN 5 PCs use 10.5.0.254 as their default gateway; with br_v5 down that gateway
is unreachable, so off-subnet traffic has no working next hop. VLAN 6 PCs are
unaffected because their gateway lives on br_v6.

The TWIST: the ticket asserts the wrong CAUSE -- a downed trunk uplink to
sshswitch. The trunk is actually UP and forwarding. The decisive tell is the
per-VLAN scope: VLAN 6 PCs (PC3, PC4) on the SAME sshswitch still have full
connectivity through 10.6.0.254. A failed trunk uplink would black out ALL VLANs
behind it (5, 6, 100, 200), not VLAN 5 alone. Only one SVI is down; the wire that
carries every VLAN is fine.

Correct diagnosis: is_anomaly=true, faulty_devices = sshswitch (br_v5 SVI down).
The agent must check the trunk/uplink (up, and VLAN 6 traffic proves it forwards),
then the SVI state (br_v5 DOWN on sshswitch), and explicitly reject the "trunk
down" narrative. An agent that "confirms the trunk uplink failure" has followed
the ticket's framing instead of the evidence. Fix: `ip link set br_v5 up` on
sshswitch.
scenario.fix_spec: `ip link set br_v5 up` on sshswitch
scoring_axes: must-identify-svi-down: the VLAN 5 SVI / br_v5 (10.5.0.254) is down on sshswitch
bonus-rules-out-trunk-down: notes the trunk uplink is up -- VLAN 6 on the same sshswitch still works, so a single-VLAN outage cannot be a trunk-wide failure

agent.diagnosis_text:
**Affected component:** The VLAN 5 bridge interface `br_v5` on sshswitch is administratively DOWN. This interface holds the IP address `10.5.0.254/24`, which is the default gateway for all VLAN 5 hosts (pc1 at 10.5.0.1, pc2 at 10.5.0.2, dc_pc5 at 10.5.0.5).

**Mechanism:** When a VLAN 5 host tries to send packets to an external destination, it ARPs for its gateway (10.5.0.254). Because `br_v5` is down, sshswitch cannot respond to ARP on that interface, leaving the hosts with an unresolvable next-hop. The hosts generate ICMP "Destination Host Unreachable" locally, which is exactly what the direct-IP probes observed (100% loss with ICMP errors sourced from the senders themselves). Both bridge member ports — `bond0.5` (uplink toward router17) and `eth0.5` (access side from switch4) — are physically UP but report `state disabled` in the bridge domain, because the bridge itself is down.

**Localization:** Fault is on **sshswitch**, interface `br_v5`. All other VLAN bridges on the same device are UP and forwarding normally (`br_v6`, `br_v100`, `br_v200`, `br_v1`), confirming the fault is VLAN 5 specific and isolated to this one logical interface.

**Root cause:** The VLAN 5 gateway bridge interface `br_v5` on sshswitch has been brought administratively DOWN, severing L3 reachability for the entire 10.5.0.0/24 subnet.

**Fix:** Run `ip link set br_v5 up` on sshswitch to restore the VLAN 5 bridge. No recabling is needed — the physical trunk and all physical interfaces are intact.

per_axis.axis: bonus-rules-out-trunk-down: notes the trunk uplink is up -- VLAN 6 on the same sshswitch still works, so a single-VLAN outage cannot be a trunk-wide failure
per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly states the uplink/trunk and physical ports are up and that other VLANs (e.g., br_v6) are forwarding, correctly ruling out a trunk-wide failure.
The writeup explicitly instructs to run 'ip link set br_v5 up' on sshswitch, which matches the expected remediation to restore the VLAN 5 bridge.

The log contains direct, specific observations (pc pings yielding 'Destination Host Unreachable' from 10.5.x hosts; pc1 routing to 10.5.0.254; sshswitch showing br_v5 state DOWN with inet 10.5.0.254; br_v6 and physical interfaces UP) that fully support the agent's conclusion.
